children: The U.S. midterm elections in November are likely to deliver a divided government, with Democrats expected to take the House, and a Democratic Senate majority looking increasingly possible, says Lombard Odier in a note. A divided government could create legislative gridlock and a mild headwind to growth over the coming quarters, it adds. While investors should expect more political friction and some market volatility around the vote, there is likely to be little change to U.S. policy and economic conditions. Trade and foreign policy will remain in the president's hands, regardless of the election results. "Whatever the election outcome, the administration will retain authority to use tariffs and other trade measures through existing executive powers, leaving the path of U.S. trade policy intact," it notes. (monica.gupta@wsj.com)
